pl-l3d34c8-d1e115.summary: Notes that Augustine's saying that chaste fear is eternal confirms the view that the spirit of fear, like the other gifts, will be in the future, but not with all its present use: it will make us revere God, not fear separation or loss.
claims: In the future fear becomes reverence.

pl-l3d34c8-d1e121.summary: Infers that this fear was in Christ in the use it will have in the saints: Christ did not fear separation or offending God, but revered him above all.
claims: Christ had fear only as reverence.

pl-l3d34c8.summary: Notes that Augustine's saying that chaste fear is eternal confirms that the spirit of fear will remain in the future like the other gifts, but with a changed use: making us revere God, not fear separation. That fear was also in Christ according to the use it will have in the saints: he did not fear separation or offending God, but revered him above all.
claims: The spirit of fear will remain in the future, as reverence.
Christ had fear in the form of reverence for God above all.
